description:
## Question

Build the two CI paths that the map 'Wayfinder: defk ready for a first Hex release' decided on, so a release never waits for the GitHub free tier.

Decided on the map (2026-10-14):
- GitHub Actions runs mix ci on every push: Linux x86-64 (clang and gcc), Linux aarch64 (clang), macOS arm64. Valgrind and the measurement run stay manual, at release time.
- The local recipe runs the same Linux matrix in Docker on the Mac: aarch64 natively, x86-64 under emulation (correct but slow; for tests, never for timing).
- A release commit needs one green run of the full matrix from either path.
- The recipe writes a short result file that the release-readiness check can cite.
- Add CC=clang on glibc to the matrix: defk-o52 crashes on the first raise without its fix (comment on defk-a1p). The Valgrind container (defk-96f.3) can become a release-time job.

Done when: the workflow is in .github/workflows/, the recipe is in the repo with a short doc, both paths ran the matrix once, and each failure is fixed or ticketed.

comments.text:
Decided with the maintainer (2026-10-14), refines the local path:
- The real work lives in one repo script (for example ci/run.sh) that runs mix ci. Each workflow job does only setup (OTP, Elixir, compiler) and then calls this script.
- act (nektos/act) is the normal local path: it runs the same .github/workflows file, so the matrix is the same by construction. Use it also to build and test the workflow before a push.
- act setup: keep the -P label mappings in a repo .actrc (ubuntu-24.04 and ubuntu-24.04-arm to images; x86-64 with --container-architecture linux/amd64 under emulation, arm64 native; macos-15=-self-hosted runs the macOS job on the Mac host). Emulation is for tests, never timing.
- Check under act and on GitHub: erlef/setup-beam (also its arm64 Linux support, from defk-wfi.1) and actions/cache. act's default images (catthehacker/ubuntu) differ from GitHub's runner images.
- Fallback that needs neither act nor GitHub: one documented docker run per matrix entry that calls the same script. A release never depends on act or on GitHub.
- The result file for the release-readiness check comes from the script, so all three paths write it the same way.

title: Dual CI: a GitHub Actions workflow and a local Docker recipe with the same matrix
